content.prompt: Determine whether these functions are odd, even, or neither.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=(-x)(-x-4)\\&=x^2+4x\end{aligned}$

This is neither $f(x)=x^2-4x$ nor $-f(x)=-x^2+4x$.

Neither odd nor even.

$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^2+1}{-x}\\&=-\frac{x^2+1}{x}\\&=-f(x)\end{aligned}$

The domain $x\ne0$ is symmetric about zero. Odd function.

$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^3}{(-x)^3-(-x)}\\&=\frac{-x^3}{-x^3+x}\\&=\frac{x^3}{x^3-x}\\&=f(x)\end{aligned}$

The domain $x\ne-1,0,1$ is symmetric about zero. Even function.

$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=\frac{-x-3}{-x+3}\\&=\frac{x+3}{x-3}\end{aligned}$

This matches neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$. Also, the domain excludes $-3$ but includes $3$, so it is not symmetric about zero.

Neither odd nor even.

$$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=2^{-x}\\&=\frac{1}{2^x}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^3}{(-x)^4-(-x)^2}\\&=\frac{-x^3}{x^4-x^2}\\&=-f(x)\end{align*}$$
The domain excludes $-1,0,1$ and is symmetric about zero. The function is odd. The DESMOS graph has rotational symmetry about the origin, including its hole at the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{1}{(-x)^3-1}\\&=\frac{1}{-x^3-1}\\&=-\frac{1}{x^3+1}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{3}{(-x)^2-4}\\&=\frac{3}{x^2-4}\\&=f(x)\end{align*}$$
The domain excludes $-2,2$ and is symmetric about zero. The function is even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{-x-3}{-x+3}\\&=\frac{x+3}{x-3}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\frac{(-x)^3}{(-x)^5-(-x)^2}\\&=\frac{-x^3}{-x^5-x^2}\\&=\frac{x^3}{x^5+x^2}\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=(-x-2)^2\\&=(x+2)^2\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about $x=2$, rather than the $y$-axis, and has no rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}-3^x\\&=-(3^x-3^{-x})\\&=-f(x)\end{align*}$$
The function is odd. The DESMOS graph has rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}+3^x\\&=3^x+3^{-x}\\&=f(x)\end{align*}$$
The function is even. The DESMOS graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=3^{-x}+(-x)^3\\&=3^{-x}-x^3\end{align*}$$
This equals neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ identically. The function is neither odd nor even. The DESMOS graph has neither symmetry about the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=(x-1)^2\\f(g(x))&=x^2-2x+1\end{align*}$$
The expression is defined for every real $x$, so the domain is $(-\infty,\infty)$. Since $(x-1)^2\geq0$, with minimum $0$ at $x=1$ and no upper bound, the range is $[0,\infty)$.

$$f(g(x))=(x+5)^3$$
The expression is defined for every real $x$, so the domain is $(-\infty,\infty)$. As $x+5$ takes every real value, its cube also takes every real value. The range is $(-\infty,\infty)$.

$$f(g(x))=\sqrt{x-2}$$
The radicand must be non-negative:
$$\begin{align*}x-2&\geq0\\x&\geq2\end{align*}$$
The domain is $[2,\infty)$. The square root has minimum $0$ at $x=2$ and no upper bound, so the range is $[0,\infty)$.

$$f(g(x))=-\sqrt{3x+9}$$
The radicand must be non-negative:
$$\begin{align*}3x+9&\geq0\\3x&\geq-9\\x&\geq-3\end{align*}$$
The domain is $[-3,\infty)$. The negative square root has maximum $0$ at $x=-3$ and no lower bound, so the range is $(-\infty,0]$.

$$f(g(x))=\sqrt{4-x^2}$$
The radicand must be non-negative:
$$\begin{align*}4-x^2&\geq0\\x^2&\leq4\\-2\leq x&\leq2\end{align*}$$
The domain is $[-2,2]$. On this domain, $4-x^2$ takes every value from $0$ to $4$, so $\sqrt{4-x^2}$ takes every value from $0$ to $2$. The range is $[0,2]$.

$$f(g(x))=-\sqrt{1-x^2}$$
The radicand must be non-negative:
$$\begin{align*}1-x^2&\geq0\\x^2&\leq1\\-1\leq x&\leq1\end{align*}$$
The domain is $[-1,1]$. On this domain, $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ takes every value from $0$ to $1$. Negating gives the range $[-1,0]$, with minimum $-1$ at $x=0$ and maximum $0$ at $x=\pm1$.

$$\begin{align*}h(f(x))&=(2x-3)^2+1\\h(f(x))&=4x^2-12x+9+1\\h(f(x))&=4x^2-12x+10\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=25-x^2$, find $f(g(x))$ and its domain.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f(g(x))&=\sqrt{25-x^2}\end{aligned}$$
The radicand must be non-negative:
$$\begin{aligned}25-x^2&\ge0\\x^2&\le25\\-5&\le x\le5\end{aligned}$$
The domain is $[-5,5]$.
The source also supplies the range. Since $0\le25-x^2\le25$ on this domain, $0\le\sqrt{25-x^2}\le5$, so the range is $[0,5]$.

MAV-11-02 uses functions and relations to model, analyse and solve problems

Properties of functions, relations and graphs
• Extend the definitions of domain and range to relations
• Recognise domains and ranges of functions and relations given in interval notation, as inequalities and as worded descriptions
• Determine and describe the domain and range of functions and relations, using interval notation, inequalities or worded descriptions
• Define a function to be even if its graph is unchanged under reflection in the y-axis, and odd if its graph is unchanged under rotation of 180° about the origin
• Develop and use the tests that a function f(x) is odd if f(−x) = −f(x) and a function f(x) is even if f(−x) = f(x)
• Solve problems involving even and odd functions
• Use the composite function f(g(x)), where the output of g(x) becomes the input of f(x)
• Determine the equations of composite functions

entries.description: Composite Functions
